newsitem.title: USA: VIVUS launches new impotence treatment.
newsitem.headline: VIVUS launches new impotence treatment.

text.p: VIVUS Inc said Monday it launched its second treatment for erectile dysfunction, the ACTIS penile band, which impedes blood flow out of the penis.
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration last December cleared ACTIS for the treatment of venous leak syndrome, the inability to trap and store blood within the penis and maintain an erection.
Vivus said the ACTIS band, which is placed at the base of the penis, is easier to use than other penile bands becase it is adjustable.
Last November, VIVUS received approval of another impotence treatment, MUSE.

Because MUSE increases inflow of penile blood and Actis decreases outflow, VIVUS said it is currently studying the use of these two treatments together for men who were unresponsive to MUSE therapy alone.
In afternoon trading, VIVUS was up 1-9/16 to 27-13/16.
